asr.full_text: Hi! This is Dr. Ken Jung of Dr. Ken and welcome to DocSupport! Ok, first question from Ashley at Kweezy Bake. How do I know if I have the stomach flue or a hangover? Well honey did you drink last night? Glug? Glug? Did you have food or did you have alcohol? The internet is not for stupidity, ma'am. The internet is for smart, established doctors like me! And my friend Louis here! Think before you Tweet. Ok, another question? Okay. Kelly underscore Sheridan won. Finally, great question. How much Vitamin C is too much? Yes, sometimes too much vitamin is too much. You always get these things on medical shows going like, Should I take this supplement? Should I take the supplement? And honestly, you can get hypervitaminosis, Like if you go to GNC or some other stores, they'll say like, oh, this is, you get like 2,000% of the recommended daily allowance of vitamin C. You can actually get side effects and symptoms or GI symptoms from too much vitamins so, it's probably good just to get like 100% of the recommended daily allowance. That's really all you need. Great question, Kelly Sheridan. I'm not supposed to pick favorites. They told me not to, the producers. But you're my favorite. BatpetitMacaroon says, I have a weird skin tag under my eye that hurts when I rip it off. What's up with that? Skin tag is called a skin polyp, in real life. It can be anywhere along your body. I think to rip off any lesion that you don't know about right under your eye. I mean honestly, I can't think of a more ill advised stupid move than that. They can numb up the area, clip it off. I've actually, when I practice medicine, someone had skin tags on their arm or extremities. You could always freeze it off with liquid nitrogen. It doesn't hurt. I highly recommend that you have a professional remove it, professionally. At Captain Handlebar asks, Now, can we address the knee reflex test at the doctor's office? This has to be useless, right? No, it's not useless. We're not monkeys that use these just for props. We're not the Carrot Top of doctors here. We're not the carrot top of doctors here. And I can just show you right here. This is the knee. There's a tendon that connects the knee to the leg bone, okay, called the tibia. There's a tendon here. You wanna check the reflex of this. You go, oh, let me just check that. And what that does, it's actually it checks really your whole nervous system in many ways to see that if your reflexes are intact, low thyroid levels in your body, which is very common called hypothyroidism, you actually will be hyporeflexic and you would not be able to elicit much of a reflex. This sucker is very important, okay? Don't mock our tools, okay. We're pros and we're sensitive, emotionally. Fizzy, so to ask, How do you check your pulse? You check it here, you check it here, even check it here on your leg. A baby could tell you how to check a pulse. Oh is, come on, anyone can ask... No, no, you can't. You can't ask any question on Twitter. Just don't defend. Shut up. I'm sorry I had to see that. It's just me and Louis got in a whole thing and whatever. Okay, moving on. Rugio Kubo says Do I really need both my kidneys? You know what, that's part of the whole area of kidney transplantation. You've heard of people donating kidneys to other people in need who have kidney failure. Technically one can survive with just one kidney if it's as long as it's normally functioning. Really good question. Hope I have more questions like this. At Haley Nesbitt1 says, why do I always get cramps or spasms in my full leg nearly every day? Hashtag ouch, hashtag Dr. Help, no sleep for me. That I would definitely get checked out. Leg pain or leg spasm can be due to a multitude of things. Instead of just saying what those hundred of things are, you actually need to see a physician for that to determine is it neurological to determine, is it neurological in nature, is it endocrinological in nature. It could be doing a lot of different things, okay, good question. At heiss-psych-EHS, quick, what are the three parts of the brain stem first one to reply with the correct answer gets a prize, study, test tomorrow, smiley emoji with glasses. Okay, so three parts of the brain stem are the medulla, the pons, and the midbrain, and the medulla, I believe, control the breathing in the pons, links the cerebellum to the cerebrum, and the midbrain read the maniovision, and hearing. Off of me, didn't have to look it up, I'm a smart man, shut up. I forget, all right, I've been busy doing hangover movies. Asshole. At, Wiggin, underscore Steven, asked, any doctors on here? Can I drink alcoholic substances while taking Erythropet antibiotics? Hashtag doctor help, hashtag doctors. You know what, actually that's a great question. Erythromycin, which is what Erythropet is a trademark name for, it can upset the stomach and also it does metabolize in the liver. So, I would check with your doctor to see exactly how much antibiotics you're taking, I generally discourage taking any alcohol while on antibiotics because a lot of antibiotics are metabolized in the liver, you don't wanna like overload them with too much things that can be toxic to your liver. All right, Faising14 asks, what's the part of the brain that's gonna deal with my emotional breakdown tomorrow, hashtag AP psyked. There's many parts of your brain that's gonna deal with my emotional breakdown tomorrow? Hashtag AP psych. There's many parts of your brain that's gonna be dealing with kinda stress to take a test, so I wish you the best of luck and I know you'll do well. Alright. At Stu Bunny asks, if anyone has any ideas for how to deal with sinus patech and pressure, I'm open to hearing it. If it's been going on for weeks at a time, I would actually consider antibiotics, and I would consider going to your general practice doctor or even an ear, nose, throat doctor, an ENT doctor to get treatment. At Dr. Claire Kane says, help, need emergency hook up cure before clinic starts in approximately five minutes. Ahhhh! See, scared you, all right? At Lifestepits, why is my eye twitching? Oh my God, stop. First of all, probably stop using words like, Oh my God, stop. Maybe get some more sleep, drink less caffeine. All right, next. I don't know, I don't know not your diaphragm. Is drinking a lot of water a bad thing? Are there any doctors on here? Actually drinking too much water can lead to some problems, I would actually go see your doctor and get your sodium level checked. Because you don't want have too too much hyponatremia. Anyway, that is doctor support. I'm Dr. Ken Jeong of Dr. Ken and I would like to thank some of you on twitter for your amazing questions and the others, you suck. You really do. Shut up, Louis, they do.
